achievement--firstDisabledMeasurement: Mark your temperature as a 'Excluding temp.' in the app if you are sick, hungover or have slept differently.
achievement--firstDisabledMeasurement--m:
# Your first excluded temperature

You just added an excluded temperature for the first time which helps maintain a high data quality.

Sickness, an excess of alcohol, and sleeping differently than usual can affect your basal body temperature which can make it harder for the algorithm to accurately detect your ovulation.

If you have any of these symptoms, you should always indicate it in the app when adding your temperature. The algorithm will then exclude it from its calculations. 

An excluded temperature will be displayed with a strike-through and will not be visible in your graph.
achievement--firstTemperatureMeasurement: Sync your temperature first thing in the morning and add the value into the app.

# First temperature entry

We are excited to see that you have now added a temperature reading for the first time! 

Remember to measure first thing in the morning, before you get up and out of bed. 🤓

There are many more [achievements](/insights/added-data/achievements) waiting to be accomplished throughout your Natural Cycles journey.

achievement--lhRecommendation--msg: # Take an ovulation test today 🎉 We recommend taking an ovulation test (LH test) today. Yay! The days you should take an ovulation test are indicated in the calendar view by this symbol: :lhtest: Natural Cycles uses temperature as the primary indicator for ovulation, but taking ovulation tests, although not mandatory, can help you get more green days. If you don't have any ovulation tests yet, you can order some from our [shop](https://www.naturalcycles.com/store/). Before taking a test, have a look at our Ovulation test guide and read the instructions on the packet carefully.
achievement--lhRecommendation-plan--msg: # Take an ovulation test today 🎉 We recommend taking an ovulation test (LH test) today. Yay! The days you should take an ovulation test are indicated in the calendar view by this symbol: :lhtest: Natural Cycles uses temperature as the primary indicator for ovulation, but taking ovulation tests, although not mandatory, can help the algorithm identify your most fertile days even faster. If you don't have any ovulation tests yet, you can order some from our [shop](https://www.naturalcycles.com/store/). Before taking a test, have a look at our Ovulation test guide and read the instructions on the packet carefully.
achievement--lhResult: Know when your ovulation is approaching by detecting an LH surge through a positive ovulation test.
achievement--lhResult--msg:
# Now we are getting to know you even better

You've logged a positive ovulation test, congratulations! A positive ovulation test detects a surge in luteinizing hormone and can give the algorithm a helping hand when confirming ovulation and getting to know your unique cycles.

On top of a positive test, the algorithm needs to detect a sufficient rise in temperature to confirm that ovulation happened—so please keep measuring!

achievement--ovulation--msg: # New achievement: Ovulation Hurray, we detected your ovulation for the first time! It will be indicated in your calendar and graph by this symbol: :ovulation: This is a **huge milestone** in your Natural Cycles journey! 💜 Tap here to see more achievements that are waiting to be accomplished.

You can order pregnancy tests from our [shop](https://www.naturalcycles.com/store/).

We are delighted for you!

You can now use the app in 'Follow your pregnancy' mode which will guide you through your pregnancy. You will get information about the development stages of your baby and useful advice on nutrition, exercise, and more.

We recommend booking an appointment with your doctor to ensure that you and your baby get off to a good start.

alert-ovulation--OVU_NOT_CONFIRMED--mess: This can happen when the algorithm needs more data, or if there is not enough of a change in your basal body temperature.
alert-ovulation--OVU_PREDICTION--message: Your ovulation is predicted by the app’s algorithm. Prediction takes different factors into account, such as historical data, ovulation test results and sign up info.
alert-ovulation--OVU_WAITING--message: An increased temperature indicates ovulation. This may take a few days to confirm, or may take until the end of your cycle. Until then you will have red days and must use protection or abstain.

anonymous-intro-p:
This added layer of protection separates your personal and fertility data.

Note! This additional layer is on top of our existing privacy protection program, NC° Secure.

apple-health-integration-body:
You may choose to import data from your Apple Health app to your NC° account and/or to export data from your NC° account to your Apple Health app. Please note that any data that you choose to export to your Apple Health app will be subject to the relevant Apple privacy policies, rather than our privacy policy.

**What's the benefit of importing data from Apple Health?**

We’ll get to know your cycle faster if we can access past fertility data including:
- Menstruation dates
- Ovulation test results

**What’s the benefit of exporting data to Apple Health?**

This is a useful way to keep your health data in one place. It can also be a handy backup if you lose access to your NC° account.

We couldn’t read any data from Apple Watch. This may happen if:

- Your watch wasn’t worn overnight, or it wasn’t properly positioned on your wrist
- Your **sleep schedule** wasn’t set (fix this via **Sleep** in the Apple Health app)
- **Sleep Focus** wasn’t enabled on your Apple Watch before you went to bed, or it was enabled for less than 4 hours
- You’re wearing an Apple Watch without temperature sensors

  • Sleep data is needed for our algorithm to pinpoint your resting temperature

You can also try wearing your watch on your inner wrist. Some users find it more comfortable and it can give you more stable temperature readings due to the increased blood flow in this area. We recommend switching wrist positions at the start of your cycle.

consent-marketing-social-info:
We use tools that help us identify and reach out to existing and new customers, by matching cookies, device identifiers and hashed (a pseudonymization technique) email addresses of people who have been using our Services with people on social media platforms to create so called “Custom Audiences” (this enables us to send targeted ads to people who have been using our Services), and “Lookalike Audiences” (this enables us to send targeted ads to people who have similar traits to our Custom Audience).

The social media platforms will not share the hashed email address with third parties or other advertisers and will delete it promptly after the match process is complete. Please note that we do not share any Sensitive Data or group users based on sensitive data for the purpose of Custom and Lookalike Audiences.

drawer-privacy-choices-body:
Please see our [US Privacy Notice Addendum](https://www.naturalcycles.com/other/legal/privacy#us-privacy-notice) for more information about how we handle your personal information and additional types of privacy requests that may be available to you.

**Opt-out of sale/sharing**

We do not sell personal information in the traditional sense of the word, for monetary consideration. However, because the definitions of “sale” and “sharing” under certain US laws may be broad enough to include the disclosure of your information to certain types of advertising and marketing partners, we allow consumers to opt-out of any such sale or sharing of their personal information. You may exercise this opt-out for this app on the app settings page “[Consent and permissions](/settings/consent)” by setting the toggle for “Social Media Partners” to the left so that it is deactivated inside of the Natural Cycles app. If you use our website, you may exercise this opt-out for our website in its [Cookie Preferences](https://www.naturalcycles.com/other/legal/cookies) by setting the toggle for “Marketing Cookies” to the left so that it is deactivated.

**Limit the use and disclosure of Sensitive Personal Information**

We use Sensitive Personal Information (as described in our [US Privacy Notice Addendum](https://www.naturalcycles.com/other/legal/privacy#us-privacy-notice)). You may request to limit our use of your Sensitive Personal Information to what is necessary to perform the services that we provide to you and as allowed under applicable law. Please visit our [privacy request webform](https://www.naturalcycles.com/submitrequest) to submit a request to limit the use and disclosure of your Sensitive Personal Information.

garmin-account-your-account-info:
You have connected your NC° account with your Garmin account to import data from your Garmin account to the Natural Cycles app. These data imports happen automatically when you open your Garmin app each day. If you would like to terminate this data import from Garmin to Natural Cycles, please click “Disconnect Garmin account” below.

This is a one-way integration, which means that any data you log on the Natural Cycles app will not sync with the Garmin app. Always refer to the NC° app for Daily Fertility Status.

When your accounts are connected, Garmin and NC° may share limited account information to help troubleshoot and resolve technical issues.

When a temperature is excluded, this means that the NC° Fertility Algorithm won’t take that night’s data into account when calculating your fertility status. 

Reasons for this include:
- If your temperature is unusually high or low — for example, if you have a fever 
- If you have fewer than four hours of continuous sleep in a night

If your sleeping heart rate is unusually high or low, it’s likely that your temperature may also have been affected. If this is the case, the NC° Fertility Algorithm will adjust it. 

If you’re feeling hungover or sick, you should manually exclude your temperature in the app.

You’ll see *Not enough data* if there isn’t enough temperature and/or heart rate data available from Oura.

This can happen if:
- You didn’t wear your ring while you slept
- The ring wasn’t properly positioned on your finger. 
- The ring didn’t have enough battery

In these cases, the NC° Fertility Algorithm won’t take that night’s data into account when calculating your fertility status

You’ll see *Interrupted sleep* if a night’s sleep wasn’t long enough for your Oura Ring to record temperature trends or heart rate data.

In this case, the NC° Fertility Algorithm won’t take that night’s data into account when calculating your fertility status. 

While it’s not always possible, try to get at least three hours of continuous sleep per night while wearing your ring. This will help you to get the most out of using Natural Cycles.

info-effectiveness-body: Natural Cycles is 93% effective with typical use, which means that 7 women out of 100 get pregnant during 1 year of use. Using the app perfectly, i.e. if you never have unprotected intercourse on red days, Natural Cycles is 98% effective, which means that 2 women out of 100 get pregnant during 1 year of use.
info-goal--PERIMENOPAUSE:
## NC° Perimenopause

Choose NC° Perimenopause if you believe you are experiencing changes related to the hormonal shifts leading up to menopause, or if you've reached menopause for medical reasons and are experiencing symptoms.

This mode is designed to help you navigate perimenopause with clarity and confidence. The NC° Menopause Algorithm estimates what stage of perimenopause you’re in. You can log symptoms, cycle data, lifestyle factors, emotions, and more. 

NC° Perimenopause will provide advanced analysis, actionable insights, and science-backed information to help you spot patterns, understand your body’s changes, and feel empowered through this period. You’ll be able to download a PDF of your Cycle Report, to make it easier to share your experience with your doctor.

NC° Perimenopause includes a fertility status, so you can still use it to prevent pregnancy. Your data is saved between modes, and you can switch back if you decide this mode isn’t for you.
info-goal--PLAN:
## NC° Plan Pregnancy

Choose NC° Plan Pregnancy if you want to get pregnant. By tracking your cycle, this mode helps you pinpoint your most fertile days to maximize your chances of conceiving.

Your daily fertility is shown in a color-coded scale in the app, so you can easily see the best time to try for a baby.
info-goal--POSTPARTUM:
## NC° Postpartum

Choose NC° Postpartum if you recently gave birth and would like to get support during your recovery process.

NC° Postpartum guides you through the physical and mental recovery after childbirth with accessible resources tailored to help promote your overall health and well-being during this crucial transition period.

Taking your temperature is not required, but measuring is encouraged as it helps our algorithm detect when your fertility returns. Until the NC° app detects your ovulation, it will give you Red Days.
info-goal--PREGNANT:
## NC° Follow Pregnancy

Choose NC° Follow Pregnancy if you are already pregnant and would like to monitor your pregnancy.

Natural Cycles will guide you through your pregnancy by providing useful information about the changes happening in your body and the development of your unborn baby.
info-goal--PREVENT:
## NC° Birth Control

Choose NC° Birth Control if you want to use Natural Cycles to prevent pregnancy. On Red Days, you are likely to be fertile, and are at risk of becoming pregnant. On these days you should use protection (such as condoms) or abstain from sex. On Green Days, you can have unprotected sex as you are not fertile.

Red and Green Days are shown in the Today view in the app with red or green colored circles.
info-green-days-body:
This percentage is based on the number of red and green days that you had in your last cycle. The number of green days you get is based on the amount of data that you add, and the amount of time the algorithm has had to get to know you.

## Effectiveness of the app

The app’s effectiveness will not change if you do not add data, but you are likely to receive more red days as a result. This is because the algorithm is designed to be cautious and give red days if it doesn’t have enough data to confirm fertility.
info-health-data-analyse:
To calculate your fertility status our algorithm will analyze the following:

* Temperature
* Period
* Spotting (bleeding that is not a menstrual period)
* Ovulation test results
info-health-data-body:
The Natural Cycles app will inform you when and if you are fertile based on the data you add to it. If you use the app to track a pregnancy, the app will provide you with information about the pregnancy. It follows from the nature of our services that we must process such data that you add to the services to enable and provide them. Below we have listed some examples of sensitive data that we need for this purpose. For more detailed information on our processing of your personal data, please see our privacy policy.

To calculate your fertility status

Our algorithm will calculate your fertility status based on an analysis of the health data that you provide, such as temperature, menstruation and ovulation test results.

To provide pregnancy information

If you are tracking a pregnancy, our app will provide information about the pregnancy based on the health data that you add, such as pregnancy test results.

To determine the App’s Pearl Index

Intercourse data is collected and displayed for our users’ convenience, but it is also an important piece of information when determining our overall Pearl Index rate (a calculation used to estimate the effectiveness of birth control).
info-health-data-pregtest-body: Natural Cycles will use pregnancy test results to analyze your cycle and calculate your pregnancy status.
info-health-data-sex-body: When you log sex, Natural Cycles will save it to be able to display it in the app.
info-health-data-title: How we use your sensitive personal data

info-lh-scanner-body:
We built the Ovulation Test Reader feature because we know it can be difficult to read ovulation test results. Our aim was to create an easy-to-use feature that could remove human bias and make taking ovulation tests simpler. 

The technology behind the Ovulation Test Reader is an algorithm that has been trained with real life ovulation test data, and has analyzed thousands of images. The algorithm uses image recognition to analyze each image you add, and then suggests a result based on its data. The Reader has been shown to be 93% accurate at identifying correct test results. 

Keep in mind that as with taking ovulation tests, using this feature is optional and you can still add your own results if you prefer.
info-lh-scanner-title: How does the Ovulation Test Reader work?
info-noLongerPregnant-body:
If you are no longer pregnant, you can select this option on the Add Data page. You can resume using Natural Cycles as you have done before. Keep in mind the app may need time to learn the pattern of your unique cycle. 

If you have questions or concerns and would like to speak to our [Support Team](https://help.naturalcycles.com/hc/en-us/requests/new?utm_source=NCApp), please reach out to us.
info-not-enough-data--APPLE_WATCH--body:
You’ll see *No data* shown in the app when temperature data isn’t available. 

This can happen if:
* You didn’t wear your watch while you slept, or it wasn’t properly positioned on your wrist
* Your watch ran out of battery
* Your **sleep schedule** wasn’t set (fix this via **Sleep** in the Apple Health app)
* **Sleep Focus** wasn’t enabled on your Apple Watch before you went to bed, or it was enabled for less than four hours
* You’re wearing an Apple Watch without temperature sensors

In this case, the NC° Fertility Algorithm won’t take that night’s data into account when calculating your fertility status.

# Is my Apple Watch compatible?

Please note: In order to measure with Apple Watch your watch must have a temperature sensor.
info-pregTestFollow-body: If you need to, you can add pregnancy test results to the app while following a pregnancy. If you input a negative test result, you will be automatically switched out of NC° Follow Pregnancy and can continue using the app to either plan or prevent pregnancy.
info-pregnancy-weeks-body:
As for the due date, we calculate the week you are at from the day of your ovulation, which is the actual date of conception. The health care system, however, always counts from the first day of your last period, as they don’t know when you ovulated.

To match how your doctor or midwife will count, the Natural Cycles algorithm automatically adds 2 additional pregnancy weeks.
info-red-days-body:
On red days – indicated by a red outlined status circle – you are very likely to be fertile and at risk of becoming pregnant.

Use protection (such as condoms or another form of barrier protection) or abstain in order to prevent a pregnancy. Red days are indicated by a red outlined circle.
info-research-library-body:
## Peer-reviewed research  
Getting our studies peer-reviewed means they are evaluated by independent experts in women’s health to ensure the findings are unbiased and accurate.

## Data insights  
With our users’ consent we can use anonymous data to gather unique learnings in the field of female health. This is our own research and is not published.
info-settings-cyclerStatus--1--txt:
You're a Newbie Cycler at the moment. The ultimate Cycler status is Star Cycler! But first you need to reach Junior, Skilled and Pro Cycler statuses!

The next step for you is to become a Junior Cycler, which will happen once the app has found your ovulation for the first time. This can take some time in the beginning while the app is getting to know you. Just keep measuring your temperature as often as possible and you’ll get there.

If you used NC° Plan Pregnancy and have become pregnant, congratulations! You will have the very special status of Preggo Cycler.
info-settings-cyclerStatus--2--txt:
You are now a Junior Cycler and the next step in the journey is to become a Skilled Cycler. 😎

You will get there just by continuing to use the app, but if you are curious about exactly what's needed, we can reveal that you need to add data at least half of the time over 3 cycles. You should also have a stable temperature variation.

You can always check your cycle statistics and view info on your temperatures in [My cycle](/insights).
info-settings-cyclerStatus--3--txt:
You are now a Skilled Cycler, the next step for you is to become a Pro Cycler. 🤓

To achieve this you need to complete at least 6 cycles, of which 5 cycles have a detected ovulation and 2 cycles with a positive ovulation test. You also need to enter data half the time with a stable temperature variation.

You can always check your cycle statistics and details on your temperatures and ovulation tests in [My cycle](/insights).
info-settings-cyclerStatus--4--txt:
You are now a Pro Cycler, which means that you're really close to becoming a Star Cycler! 💫

To achieve this you, need to be an ambassador by referring 10 friends with your personal link. If they sign up via your link, they'll get a 20% discount on the NC° Annual Plan and a free basal thermometer — plus you'll get a reward for every friend you refer.

Once 10 of your friends have signed up with your link, you'll become a Star Cycler and get a free lifetime subscription to Natural Cycles. So share with all of your friends! 

Get your personal link and check the status of your referrals on your [Referrals](/refer) page.
info-stis-body:
Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are diseases that are spread by having sex with someone who has an STI.

Natural Cycles does not protect against sexually transmitted infections. Use a condom to protect against STIs.
info-store-data-body: If you terminate your account with us, we will keep your User Data for an additional 3 years. The reason is to give you the possibility to come back at a different stage in your life and pick up on the data you had then. You always have the right to request your data to be deleted earlier. When we no longer have a reason to keep your Personal Data, if you withdraw your consent or if you successfully request that we erase it, we have processes in place for anonymizing your Personal Data.

While it’s not always possible, try to get at least three hours of continuous sleep per night while wearing your ring. This will help you to get the most out of using Natural Cycles.

[Visit the Oura help pages to find out more.](https://support.ouraring.com/)
info-typical-use-body: The Typical Use Pearl Index of a birth control method estimates how many women (out of 100) will become pregnant during one year.
info-unplanned-pregnancy-weeks-body:
Pregnancy weeks are calculated from the day of conception. Your conception date is the day you ovulated in your last menstrual cycle, as this is the day the sperm and egg cells met.

Doctors and midwives count pregnancy weeks from the first day of your last period, as they can’t confirm when you ovulated. To match this way of counting, our algorithm automatically adds 2 extra pregnancy weeks.
insights-modal-irregular-cycle-length: Your cycle length is **irregular**. That means that the length of your cycle tends to be 20 days or shorter, or 36 days or longer (outside the medical norm).
insights-modal-irregular-cycle-length-an: Both your cycle length and variation are **irregular**. That means that the length of your cycle tends to be 20 days or shorter, or 36 days or longer, and that it also tends to vary from your average by 8 or more days from cycle to cycle (outside the medical norms).
insights-modal-irregular-cycle-variation: Your cycle length variation is **irregular**. That means that the length of your cycle tends to vary from your average by 8 or more days from cycle to cycle (outside the medical norm).
insights-modal-irregular-long-follicular: Your follicular phase length is **irregular**. That means that your follicular phase tends to last for 26 days or more.
insights-modal-irregular-luteal-length: Your luteal phase length is **irregular**. That means that your luteal phase tends to be 9 days or shorter.
insights-modal-irregular-ovulation: 3 or more **anovulatory cycles** were detected in the past 12 months. Our bodies skip ovulation occasionally, but recurrent anovulation is worth monitoring.
insights-modal-irregular-period-length: Your period length is **irregular**. That means that your period tends to last for 8 days or longer.
insights-modal-irregular-short-follicula: Your follicular phase length is **irregular**. That means that your follicular phase tends to last for 10 days or less.
insights-modal-regular-cycle: Your cycle is regular. This means that both your cycle length and variation (how much it changes from cycle to cycle) are considered normal by medical standards.
integration-benefits-body--GARMIN_WATCH:
By connecting your Garmin account with the NC° app, you’re enabling us to import key data. Please note that this data sharing is one way and no data is shared back to Garmin from your NC° account. **What data is required and why?** - Temperature data is needed to calculate your fertility status - Heart rate data helps us detect changes so we can adjust for your lifestyle **Importing data from Garmin Connect**
To integrate with your Garmin wearable we need to import the following data: - Women’s Health - Daily Health Stats Allowing access to these ensures that NC° can process all the essential metrics to provide a fertility status and other insights.
integration-benefits-body--OURA:
By connecting your Oura account with the NC° app, you’re enabling us to import key data. Please note that this data sharing is one way and no data is shared back to Oura from your NC° account.

**Importing data from Oura Cloud**</br>
We can get to know your cycle faster and provide more fertility insights if we can import certain types of data including:
- Temperature trends
- Heart rate
- Logged periods

When enabling permissions, you may find it useful to know that temperature trend and heart rate data are categorized as **“Sleep, Readiness and Activity Data”**, whereas logged periods are counted as **“Tag Data”**.
integration-benefits-body--WHOOP_BAND: By connecting your WHOOP account with the NC° app, you’re enabling us to import key data. Please note that this data sharing is one way and no data from your NC° account is shared back to WHOOP. Importing data from WHOOP To integrate with your wearable, you’ll be asked to allow access the following data: - Cycles - Profile - Recovery - Sleep Why is this data required? The imported data includes temperature and heart rate data. The NC° app uses it to calculate your fertility status and detect changes so we can adjust for your lifestyle. Allowing access ensures that NC° can process all the essential metrics to provide a reliable fertility status and other insights.

mom-text--10:
Your belly is getting slightly rounder (and clothes slightly tighter). Your body is starting to change to make space for your growing uterus, which is now about the size of a pomegranate. You might start noticing a more visible network of veins under your skin, especially on your belly
and your breasts. It’s your circulatory system that expands to provide a sufficient blood flow for the fast growth of your fetus. The blue streaks will only remain until the end of your pregnancy, or until you stop breastfeeding.

On the side, you probably still have to deal with the well-known pregnancy symptoms, such as nausea, fatigue, mood swings, constipation, frequent urination. For most mothers-to-be these
sources of discomfort are about to get better, so hold on a little longer! 💪 Keep your meals simple, light and frequent, drink plenty, do some light exercise, and rest as much as you can.
mom-text--11:
Inside your body things keep changing. So it is no surprise that you might feel unusually tired and sleepy at any time of the day, and you might find it hard to focus at work or even just at simple tasks in your daily routine. Take it easy, sleep plenty, and try to rest when your body
needs it 💤

Your uterus is making space to accommodate not only your baby, but also the amniotic sac and the placenta, which started developing in the first few weeks after implantation, and grew along with the embryo. The placenta is a temporary organ designed to provide the baby with oxygen, water, and nutrients, to manage the waste produced by the baby’s functions, and to produce many of the hormones needed during the pregnancy. At the same time, it stops most bacteria
and viruses from entering the blood circulation of the fetus, acting as a barrier and protecting it from diseases. What an amazing organ the placenta is! 👏
mom-text--12:
This is the last week of the first trimester 🙌 though it might still be hard to tell from the outside that you’re expecting. With a little bit of luck your morning sickness is starting to fade, and your energy levels are slowly getting back to what it used to be before the pregnancy. If that’s not the case yet, be patient and wait, as it might just happen a little later.

In case you have decided to wait with sharing the good news with family and friends, you might feel that the time has come, as risks of miscarriage or fetal malformation are significantly reduced at the end of the first trimester. Some couples instead shout it out loud from the
beginning, others prefer to wait until the end of the first trimester. When and how to share the news is totally up to you!

In any case you probably won’t be able to hide your baby from the world for much longer: your bump will start showing soon! 🤰
mom-text--13:
Congratulations! You are 1⁄3 done with your pregnancy
🎉

At this stage some of the symptoms of the first trimester are probably behind you, which doesn’t mean that your pregnancy hormones are quiet now. In the last few weeks their production has been mostly taken over by the placenta.

Although most women are feeling relieved that the nausea has quieted down by now, some unlucky few might not be out of the woods just yet. If you have been experiencing excessive vomiting and cannot manage to keep your food down and the symptoms are not getting better
by now, you may have hyperemesis gravidarum. Although this is not directly dangerous to the mother or baby, it may come with dehydration or weight loss, so do talk to your doctor if you think you may be experiencing this.
mom-text--14:
You are now entering the second trimester of your pregnancy! For most women this is the most enjoyable part. It has sometimes even been called the “honeymoon phase” of pregnancy. Morning sickness should be less of a burden now, and you should be able to enjoy the return of
your normal appetite. Try to still stick to healthy and nutritious meals, and to limit greasy and highly processed foods, as your body and the baby need a lot of nutrients right now 🥦

As the belly is now becoming more prominent, experts advise to sleep on the side from the second trimester on 🛌This is due to the fact that sleeping on your back might cause the belly to push on some of the major veins and intestines and reduce blood circulation, which can make you feel dizzy.
mom-text--15:
Although you should feel quite a lot better than during the first trimester, you might start noticing other minor annoyances that typically show up at the beginning of the second trimester.
As a side effect of the high estrogen and progesterone levels, many women develop some sort of irritation to the gums, with swollen, inflamed tissue and frequent bleeding. 

You can minimise discomfort by brushing your teeth after every meal with a softer toothbrush, using gentle mouth washes, flossing every day, and avoiding chewy sweets that tend to stick to your teeth. It is also a good idea to organise an appointment with your dentist during pregnancy, if you haven’t yet done so. But don’t worry too much: if you had good dental health before pregnancy, it will most likely go back to normal after you give birth to your baby.
mom-text--16:
Among all the other changes, you might start noticing that your pregnancy is affecting your skin as well. This is due to the same pregnancy hormones that are responsible for a good deal of the
typical symptoms you are going through. The increased blood flow might make you feel flushed at times, and give your cheeks a rosy look. At the same time, the hormones stimulate your skin to produce more oil and to retain more moisture, which tend to smoothen your wrinkles. For
many women, the “pregnancy glow” is definitely not a myth!

On the other hand, there are negative side effects along with the good ones. Your skin tends to become more delicate and irritable. Acne and spots are common, too. To minimize the effect try to wash your face with gentle soap on a regular basis but not too frequently, and stick to water-based skin products for cleansing and makeup.
mom-text--17:
The pregnancy glow - and a more unwelcomed come back of the spots you used to have when you were 14 - are not the only changes happening to your skin.

The fluctuating hormone levels affect the production of melanin, the brown pigment that determines the color of skin and hair. More melanin means that your skin tends to become darker, especially in areas around your nipples and belly button, and you might develop patches
on your face and neck. A dark vertical line - called linea nigra - usually appears on your belly between your breasts and your pelvis. Although patches and lines usually disappear after you give birth, you can try to protect your skin by applying sunscreen and by limiting the time you
spend in the sun 😎

Another side effect of growing a baby can be stretch marks that appear as your belly, breasts, and thighs expand. About 9 in 10 women get these, so you are certainly not alone. Also the stretch marks will fade as your body recovers after giving birth.
mom-text--18:
Your uterus keeps expanding to accommodate the growth of your baby. Soon it will no longer fit within your pelvis, so it will need to gradually stretch up to your navel, and eventually all the way up to your breasts.

Besides doctor appointments, the size of your belly will probably become a topic of conversation with your family, friends, and sometimes even total strangers. As irritating as this may be, try not
to stress about the changes you see in your body, and to relax instead into your new shape as a visible sign of the happiness to come!

By now you might already be feeling your baby moving 🚼 These first fetal movements are called “quickening” and are often described as flutters. It may be difficult to determine whether this feeling is gas or your baby’s movements, but soon you will begin to notice a pattern. If you are a second-time mom, you might already have been feeling it for a few weeks now.
mom-text--19:
Most women feel quite good at this stage in pregnancy, as the discomforts of the first trimester are long gone. Your appetite is back together with your energy, and the mood swings are less extreme.

Another good aspect is the increased sex drive! 🐇 In some women the pregnancy hormones actually tend to boost libido and make sex more pleasant, as the vulva and clitoris become more sensitive. If you as a couple feel like it, there is no reason to abstain, unless explicitly
discouraged by your doctor. Sex is perfectly safe throughout the whole pregnancy, and it even seems to have benefits for your health. 

It’s also a wonderful way to relax and to strengthen your connection with your partner in this very special time of your lives.
mom-text--20:
Around this time, you should have the mid-pregnancy prenatal checkup. This is when your health care professional makes sure that the fetus is healthy and is developing normally. They measure your belly and weigh you, but most importantly they perform an ultrasound called the
anomaly or anatomy scan. They usually examine the fetal position, brain, heart chambers and heartbeat, spine and vertebrae, face, and movements, in order to exclude malformations that might cause complications during the pregnancy and after birth. 

They also look at the size and position of the placenta and measure the amount of amniotic fluid. At this point they will also be able to reveal the sex of the baby, unless you prefer to keep the surprise 🎊At the end you get to walk home with some of the very first pictures of your little one!
mom-text--21:
Congratulations! You’re now in the second half of your pregnancy! Twenty weeks left until you get to meet the new little member of the family 🐣

At this point you probably have had your mid-pregnancy prenatal checkup, if not it will most likely happen soon. If all went well you have seen your healthy little baby moving in your uterus, listened to his/her heartbeat, and discovered whether you’ll be having a boy or a girl, unless you decided to keep it a surprise.

By now you have probably felt the baby’s movements, first as a fluttering and then stronger and stronger (but don’t get worried if you haven’t yet). The arrival of your child feels more and more
real! This is the time when many mothers-to-be feel the most comfortable.
mom-text--22:
If you are not expecting twins or triplets there should now be about 20 to 25 cm between your pubic bone and the top of your uterus. At this stage the increased weight of your uterus already puts quite a bit of pressure to your pelvic floor 🏋♀

The pelvic floor is a net of muscles, ligaments, and other tissues in the lower part of your abdomen, between your pubic bone and your spine. The pelvic floor normally supports your inner organs, and allows you to control your bladder and bowel. During pregnancy it naturally
stretches and becomes weaker, which might create complications during childbirth, and make the recovery more difficult. It is therefore a good idea to do certain exercises (Kegel exercises) to strengthen your pelvic floor, early on in your pregnancy.
mom-text--23:
Your bump is growing and will soon get in your way when you move, sit and sleep. The extra weight will start stressing your body, and backaches are one of the most common effects. There are a few tricks to make your life a bit more comfortable and reduce pain. Instead of slouching, try to sit straight with your back resting on the chair or on a pillow, and your legs apart.

 When you pick up something from the floor, put one leg to the front and bend your knees rather than bowing with your legs straight. Try to avoid lifting heavy weights, although this might be difficult depending on your job, or if you already have a little one at home! Exercises can also help strengthening and relaxing your muscles 🧘♀
mom-text--24:
Your belly keeps growing. As the baby has become tighter in your uterus you should have started perceiving his/her movements in the uterus. The initial feeling of fluttering that could have been mistaken for gas, is probably much more clear now. You might have also started noticing a certain pattern, with peaks of activity in the evening and early night, and more quiet times during the day when you are the most active. The fetus usually has sleep cycles that are about 45 minutes long, so it is normal not to feel any movements for such periods. 

Try to pay attention to your baby’s activity, and to get familiar with his/her pattern, as the way the fetus moves in the uterus is a good indicator of his/her wellbeing. If by the end of this week you haven’t felt any hint of movement, get in touch with your doctor or midwife, as they might want to visit you and perform some additional tests to ensure that you and the fetus are in good health. Contact them as soon as possible in case you suddenly notice a change in your baby’s activity.
mom-text--25:
Around this time you might start experiencing the so-called “false labour” -- or Braxton-Hicks contractions -- a tightening of the uterine muscles, between 20 seconds to a couple of minutes long. This is quite normal, and not necessarily a sign that your body is about to get ready to give birth. The contractions usually appear quite early in the pregnancy, while most women only notice them as they become more intense in the second half of their pregnancy, and some never do.

Braxton-Hicks contractions can be told apart from real preterm labour as they are usually quite infrequent, irregular, and painless, although they can become quite uncomfortable. If you are worried about the possibility of preterm labour, try to time the contractions for about an hour. If you notice them becoming more regular, frequent, stronger and more painful over time, and if they do not respond to a change in position, or if you have other signs or symptoms such as bloody vaginal discharge, or back pain, get in touch with your doctor or midwife.
mom-text--26:
Your uterus and your belly keep stretching to make space for your growing baby at a fast pace. There is no evidence that creams can prevent stretch marks, but it certainly can help with the itching.

The amount of blood in your body is increasing significantly and your heart and kidneys are working hard to take care of the extra liquid in your body. If you are experiencing symptoms of fatigue and/or headaches, it might be due to low iron levels. Make sure to eat foods with high iron content such as broccoli or spinach. You might also want to talk to your doctor about taking iron supplements in case a blood test reveals too low iron levels.
mom-text--27:
Last week of the second trimester, puh! Great job!

You might sometimes be feeling a rhythmic movement in the belly and it might be your baby having hiccups 👶 It is normal and nothing to worry about.

Another, less fun, symptom that you might be experiencing now is Restless legs syndrome (RLS). For some women they have difficulties sitting still as the legs become jittery and twitching. This might be a sign of low iron levels. Yoga or other relaxation techniques might help a little.
mom-text--28:
Congratulations, another trimester is gone! You are now in the third and last trimester of your pregnancy. Keep up the good work! 💪

The top of your uterus should now be about 5 cm above your belly button, which might -- or might not -- eventually pop out with the pressure.

The extra volume, and weight, will make you more uncomfortable. Rest as much as you can, this is the time to take it easy and pamper yourself. It is also time to start planning for the birth and for your new life.
mom-text--29:
When it comes to pregnancy, and quite frankly being a woman in general, it’s all about the hormones 👩🔬 To prepare for birth, the hormone relaxin increases in the body during pregnancy and loosens the joints. One side effect of this can be Symphysis pubis dysfunction
(SPD). The relaxin can make the ligaments in your pelvic joint too stretchy such that it becomes unstable, which can be painful. If this is the case for you, it could help wearing a pregnancy support belt to stabilize the ligament.

Another pregnancy side effect that you might be dealing with could be swollen feet and ankles. Comfy shoes and compression socks can be of huge help. Also don’t forget to rest and sometimes put your feet up, remember - you are growing a human being inside you! 💪
mom-text--3: Before the embryo has implanted into your uterus, which usually happens around 9 days after ovulation, your body is not yet aware that it is pregnant. You will therefore not be able to feel any pregnancy symptoms or get a positive pregnancy test until a little later. We are however keeping our fingers crossed! 🤞
mom-text--30:
You might be enjoying feeling your baby on a daily basis at this stage 🚼 He or she has gotten stronger and you might feel strong kicks by now. From now on, it’s good if you can get to know the pattern of your baby’s movement and check in on the baby every day.

The closer you are to your due date, the more important regular checking of fetal movements becomes. The baby rarely sleeps more than an hour and can usually be woken up if you have a snack or a glass of orange juice. Get in touch with your practitioner if you note a sudden
decrease in movement.
mom-text--31:
Why is it so hard to sleep in the third trimester?? 💤 It can be frustrating, so we feel you! It’s not surprising though given that you might be suffering from heartburn, restless legs and having to get up to pee all the time. And of course, not to forget the bump that is getting bigger by the day and it might be difficult to find a comfortable position. Sleeping on the side is advised and some women find it comfortable to “hug” a larger pillow, putting it in between your knees and your arms 🛌

If heartburn is what’s bothering you at night, remember not to eat too close to bedtime. It might also help to sleep with a few pillows below your upper body to get a bit of an inclination as gravity then helps keep the stomach acids down.
mom-text--32:
You are now in week 32 and the end is really getting near! Your Braxton Hicks contractions are probably becoming more and more frequent, which is a great sign that your uterus is practising for the grand finale. They will continue to increase in strength and frequency as you get closer and closer to labour.

You might also have noticed your breasts increasing in size again 🍒 Some might even experience that the breasts start leaking colostrum, which is the precursor to breast milk. Colostrum is highly nutritious and full of protein and antibodies. However, since there is no baby yet to give this superfood to, leaky breast can instead be a bit annoying and it might help to wear nursing pads.
mom-text--33:
You are now in the eighth month of your pregnancy! You are just a short time away from meeting the little human being that is growing inside you 🐣 These months are exciting, but can also be impatient times!

At this pregnancy stage, your shortness of breath that you might already be experiencing is getting worse. Previously it was mainly due to the increase in hormonal levels, but by now the uterus has grown so large that it starts pushing on the diaphragm, which compresses your
lungs. 

Since your lungs are unable to fully expand when you take a breath, it causes you to feel like you've just run a marathon when you've only climbed a flight of stairs 🏃♀It feels as if you are living life at a high altitude where oxygen is sparse, like on top of a mountain ⛰
mom-text--34:
Your blood volume has increased by 40% to 50% by now and a big share of the extra blood supply is used by your ever-growing uterus. After pregnancy week 34, the blood volume only increases marginally, so check on that one, you are done producing extra blood!

The extra blood volume also comes in handy after birth, since you usually lose some of it during birth. Do you have the thickest, most amazing head of hair right now? During pregnancy you stop
shedding hair at its normal rate. Usually about 90% of your hair is growing at any given time, while the rest is in a "resting" stage, followed by falling out. 

During pregnancy, however, the higher estrogen levels extend that growth phase, meaning you lose less hair and may suddenly
find yourself with a gloriously thick ponytail. Unfortunately, this bliss will not last forever as the extra hair will fall out after pregnancy.
mom-text--35:
Although you still have a few more weeks to go, it is now a good idea to start preparing for childbirth. Get familiar with the signs of labour, so you know how to detect them and how to react if they happen a little earlier.

Remember how we told you that knowing when ovulation (conception) happened makes the prediction of your due date more accurate? Well, it turns out that the due date is based on the average time between conception and birth, but it doesn’t mean that your baby will arrive
exactly by then. Already now there is a small probability of spontaneous labour happening, but it is the most probable to happen within 2 weeks before/after your due date. 

The element of surprise can be both terrifying and quite exciting!
mom-text--36:
During this week, your uterus reaches the highest point in your body. This means that although you might feel quite uncomfortable at the moment, many of the symptoms will not get worse but rather improve in the next few weeks. It will get a little easier to breathe and to move around. 

A downside, however, might be that you might feel the urge to pee more often as the baby’s descending head is pushing on your bladder.
Speaking of going to the toilet 🚽you might be experiencing hemorrhoids, which are another joyful 😝 pregnancy side effect. (How do we women manage all this, eh?) Try to avoid constipation and remember to do your Kegel exercises to strengthen your pelvic floor in preparation for birth, as hemorrhoids may also develop postpartum as a result of pushing during labor.
mom-text--37:
You are now in the 9th and last month of pregnancy, way to go!!! 🏃♀
Do you know why you always have to leave a urine sample when you are visiting your doctor for a check up? The combination of protein in the urine and high blood pressure are signs of preeclampsia, which -- if untreated -- can lead to eclampsia and involve serious complications for
both you and the baby. Preeclampsia is the most common complication to occur during pregnancy.

It generally develops during the third trimester and affects about 1 in 20 pregnancies. Preeclampsia can often be managed with oral or IV medications until the baby is sufficiently mature to be delivered. This requires weighing the risks of early delivery versus the risks of continued preeclampsia symptoms. It is thus very important to go to all those checkups!
mom-text--38:
The final countdown is here! Only a few weeks left now, how exciting! 🤩The baby is still considered to be “early term” but it would not be completely unlikely for the baby to come out soon.
Are you ready for birth with the hospital bag packed and have you written a birth plan yet? 🗒 It might feel a little silly at first to write one, but it can really help during delivery when it might be
hard to express your thoughts and feelings. What kind of pain relief would you or would you not want? 

Do you want a lot of physical touch as encouragement or do you rather have your space? It can be a good idea to go through the birth plan with your doctor in advance to understand if there are any unrealistic expectations and/or what your doctor and/or hospital can provide for
you. It can also be a good idea to share it in advance with your partner such that they can understand what is important to you and best support you during birth. For instance many women say it helped when their partner put pressure on the lower back during painful contractions.
mom-text--39: OMG, it is happening soooon! 🍼 These last days and weeks might however feel very long. Could time pass any slower, right? It might be good to try and have the expectation that the baby will come out a little later than the due date, to not make the wait feel too long. If this is your first, this might also very well be the case 🐣
mom-text--4:
Implantation of the embryo in your uterus usually happens around 9 days after ovulation, which is also when your body starts producing the hCG hormone that can be traced through pregnancy tests. This means that your pregnancy can be detected during the later part of this
week. Congratulations! 🎉

Light bleeding (spotting) can happen as a result of the implantation of the embryo in your uterus and can be accompanied by mild cramps. This is normal, and in general nothing to worry about. If on the other hand you notice more significant bleeding, such as the one you usually experience during your period or heavier, or experience severe cramping, get in touch with your doctor.
mom-text--40:
Only one week to go until you are actually due! 😍

You might be wondering when is it happening and analyzing every sign your body is giving you. Here are a few that might be an indication that labour is approaching:

- The baby has “dropped” far down in your pelvis, which for second-time moms only
happens near birth.
- Backache and cramps, which might be an early sign that your cervix is getting softer
and maybe even started dilating
- Different/more vaginal discharge. Eventually, you might also notice the loss of your
mucus plug, which has protected your uterus and baby from infection during pregnancy.
It is a jelly sticky glob of mucus that comes out when your cervix softens and dilates
- Your water breaks. Just like with the mucus plug, this might not happen until well into
labour, but it can also happen days before labour starts. Check with your doctor when
they’d want you to come in in case your water breaks.
- More intense and frequent Braxton Hicks contractions. When the contractions start
hurting in the lower back and/or become quite regular and more painful in general, it
might actually be “real” early labour contractions. This means that it is on! 💥
mom-text--41:
No baby yet? You might be anxious to get going and meet your little miracle for the first time 👶

Although there is no miracle cure when it comes to getting your baby out (except induction by a doctor), there are a few things you can do on your own that research indicates might help a little, and at least it won’t hurt:

- Walking🚶♀Gravity + movement might help the baby move further down in your pelvis and might make it push on your cervix. Just don’t exhaust yourself, such that you don’t have enough energy for the long marathon of giving birth
- Sex ❤ If this old tale is true or not is not certain, but sperm does contain prostaglandins, a hormone that can help dilate the cervix, ripening it for delivery.
- A membrane sweep. If your cervix is at least slightly open, your doctor could perform this procedure at one of your check ups if he or she thinks that this could be a good way to speed things up. They then insert their finger up and into your cervix and sweep around to separate the membrane that surrounds your baby from the lower part of your
uterus. This can help jump-start the contractions, but it can also be quite painful 😧
mom-text--5:
Week 5 is when most women find out about their pregnancy and can be both an exciting but also an emotional time for both you and your partner. Although your hormone levels are on a steep rise, you probably don’t have any of the special symptoms of pregnancy just yet.

Natural Cycles calculates your due date from the day of your ovulation, which is the actual date of conception. Traditionally weeks are counted from menstruation, since this used to be the only data at hand 😏 so when ovulation (conception) happens, 14 days are added to the pregnancy counting. You are 4 weeks plus X days today, which is considered to be the 5th week of pregnancy, even though you and your body just found out 😅

If you haven’t already started eating prenatal vitamins, now is the time. Most important is to get an extra 400 micrograms of folic acid daily to help prevent birth defects of the fetal brain and spine called neural tube defects. Vitamin D is also important to help the fetus’s bones and teeth develop.
mom-text--6:
As your hormone levels rise you start noticing the first signs of early pregnancy in your body. Together with more than two thirds of expecting women, you might unfortunately experience
some degree of nausea and vomiting from the 6th or 7th week of pregnancy 🤢 You also become more sensitive to odors, and suddenly might feel repulsed by a dish that you loved just
a few weeks ago. This is the so-called morning sickness, although it can occur at any time of the day 😬You might also feel uncomfortably bloated and you might have to go to the bathroom
more often, due to the increased blood flow to your kidneys.

Along with the physical symptoms, your mood swings are becoming more intense, so you might end up feeling happy, anxious, angry, scared, excited, all in the same day! Depression is quite
common as well, especially at the beginning and at the end of the pregnancy, as well as after delivery. If you notice signs of depression, it might be a good idea to talk to someone about it ❤
mom-text--7:
Your body is rapidly transforming to support the fast growth of the embryo. The hCG hormone levels are rising, usually doubling every couple of days during the first ten weeks of pregnancy.
Progesterone and estrogen are also being produced, first by your ovaries, and later by the placenta. These hormones have the important tasks of transforming your uterus to host the embryo, stimulating the development of your breasts for breastfeeding, and facilitating the
development of your baby throughout the pregnancy.

The side effects of your fluctuating hormones are the signature symptoms of pregnancy, that could be loud and clear by now 😔You might feel exhausted, bloated, constipated, and moody. Your nausea probably hasn’t gotten any better either. A small comfort could be to know that most mothers-to-be start feeling better at the end of the first trimester 💜
mom-text--8:
Your hCG hormone level is still rising very rapidly, probably making your pregnancy symptoms more intense, especially if you’re expecting twins or triplets. If you are nauseous you can try out a few remedies that could make you feel a little better:

- avoid having an empty stomach - eat frequently but not too much
- eat simple starchy and salty snacks, dried fruits or nuts 🥜
- eat acid foods, such as citrus 🍋
- avoid spicy, greasy, deep fried foods
- do some light exercise if you can, like walking, swimming, or yoga 🧘♀
- drink plenty of fluids 💧

It is important that you ask your doctor before taking any medication, since many drugs, and even herbal remedies, could have an effect on your pregnancy. Reach out also in case of more severe nausea or vomiting.
mom-text--9:
Your uterus has already expanded to about twice its original size. It is a little too early to measure your belly, but you may soon have to buy a new bra as your breasts grow one cup size or two in preparation for breastfeeding. Other changes also happen - lumps might appear in the
breast tissue, your areolas -- the areas around the nipples -- get wider and darker, while little bumps become more visible 🍒 

These are glands, producing oil that facilitates breastfeeding. Your breasts may feel tingling and sore. All these changes are normal, and will continue happening throughout your pregnancy, but feel free to discuss them with your doctor if you are concerned.

my-data-cycle-highly-irregular: Your cycle is **highly irregular**. This means that the length of your cycle changes with more than seven days.
my-data-cycle-irregular: Your cycle is **irregular**. This means that the length of your cycle changes between four and seven days.
my-data-cycle-length-txt:
We consider your cycle to be regular if it’s between 21 and 35 days long, and if the length of your cycle tends to vary from your average by 7 days or less. This is the medical norm defined by the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG).

Small fluctuations in any cycle are quite common, and it’s possible to experience bigger changes when you’re sick, stressed, or have been traveling. If there are bigger fluctuations outside the medical norm for a longer duration, we’ll let you know your cycle is getting irregular.

Note that an irregular cycle does not affect the app’s effectiveness, but it’s possible you will have more Red Days.
my-data-cycle-regular: Your cycle is **regular**. This means that the length of your cycle changes with four days or less.
my-data-green-days-description: This cycle you had {{green}}% Green and {{red}}% Red Days.
my-data-green-days-plan-description: Here’s your split of fertile and non-fertile days.
my-data-lh-tests-txt:
An ovulation test helps the algorithm find your ovulation, but it is not required. Think of it as extra credit! 

The test is a stick that analyzes your urine for the Luteinizing Hormone (LH), which surges right before ovulation. A positive ovulation test does not confirm ovulation, but it helps the algorithm's calculations.

my-data-why-data-description: The more data you add, the better the algorithm gets to know you. This usually means more green days, but a varying temperature or irregular cycles can affect the number of green days you get too. The app remains as effective, but you may get more red days.

onboarding-breast-feeding-txt:
Whether a pregnancy results in birth, miscarriage or termination, the body undergoes hormonal changes that impact the cycle — it’s important we factor these in as the algorithm gets to know you.

**Important note on breastfeeding:**  
If you give birth and choose to exclusively breastfeed, be aware that you may not ovulate for 4-6 months after pregnancy. 

NC° will detect your first ovulation about two weeks before your first period, but until then you will only see Red Days in the app. 

Even though you are not ovulating, it is still important to use contraception or abstain from intercourse on Red Days.

onboarding-hbc-disclaimer-bleeding-txt: When you discontinue hormonal birth control, you may first experience a withdrawal bleed, which is much lighter than your true period. You will normally get your true period a few weeks later. Withdrawal bleeding should not be entered as “period” into the app. If you are unsure if you are experiencing withdrawal bleeding or a period, please consult your doctor.
onboarding-hbc-disclaimer-red-days-txt:
Our data show that women transitioning to Natural Cycles from hormonal birth control have a higher risk of becoming pregnant due to generally not yet being accustomed to using other forms of protection.

On red days, you must either abstain or use protection, such as condoms (or another form of barrier protection), to prevent pregnancy. If you have not been using a non-hormonal based method of birth control before, make sure to have a method on hand to use during red days, such as condoms.

It can take several cycles after discontinuing hormonal birth control before becoming more regular again. You should expect more red days during these cycles and therefore expect to use protection, such as condoms (or another form of barrier protection), or abstain more frequently.

onboarding-hormonal-type-info-body:
There are lots of different hormonal birth control methods out there. We’ve included a selection of the most commonly used options. If you can’t see your option on the list, please select “other”. 

## The pill and the mini-pill

The combined pill is commonly referred to as “the birth control pill” or “the pill”. It contains both synthetic estrogen and progesterone and is typically taken for 3 weeks with a 1-week break. The mini pill (also known as the progestogen-only pill) contains only synthetic progesterone. It’s taken every day without a break. If you are unsure what method you are using, check your pill packet or ask your doctor.

onboarding-medical-condition-warning-txt:
As a contraceptive, Natural Cycles may be less suitable for you if you have certain medical conditions that affect your cycle regularity and/or temperature as predicting fertility is more difficult in these circumstances.

Natural Cycles’ effectiveness as a contraceptive is not affected by these conditions, but you will experience an increased number of Red Days, which can reduce your satisfaction with Natural Cycles.

As a birth control, Natural Cycles may be less suitable for you if you are in Menopause, as predicting fertility is more difficult in these circumstances.

Natural Cycles’ effectiveness as a birth control is not affected by Menopause, but you will experience an increased number of Red Days, which can reduce your satisfaction with Natural Cycles.

As a birth control, Natural Cycles may be less suitable for you if you have PMOS (formerly PCOS), as predicting fertility is more difficult in these circumstances. 

Natural Cycles’ effectiveness as a birth control is not affected by PMOS, but you will experience an increased number of Red Days, which can reduce your satisfaction with Natural Cycles.

As a birth control, Natural Cycles may be less suitable for you if you have a thyroid-related condition, as predicting fertility is more difficult in these circumstances.

Natural Cycles’ effectiveness as a birth control is not affected by these conditions, but you will experience an increased number of Red Days, which can reduce your satisfaction with 
Natural Cycles.

You might notice irregularities in your cycle after you’ve stopped using hormonal birth control. It might take time for things to balance out and for your natural cycle to resume.

oura-integration-benefits-body:
By connecting your Oura account with the NC° app, you’re enabling us to import key data. Please note that this data sharing is one way and no data is shared back to Oura from your NC° account.

**Importing data from Oura Cloud**
We can get to know your cycle faster and provide more fertility insights if we can import certain types of data including:

- Temperature trends
- Heart rate
- Logged periods

When enabling permissions, you may find it useful to know that temperature trend and heart rate data are categorized as **“Sleep, Readiness and Activity Data”**, whereas logged periods are counted as **“Tag Data”**.

past-data-import-current-phase-descripti: As you enter the fertile window, you may feel at your best. This point in the cycle is a good time for challenging tasks, or more intense workouts.
You may feel tired or experience other PMS symptoms. To support your body, try eating whole foods, avoiding caffeine and choosing moderate or gentle exercise. Remember to be kind to yourself.
At this point in your cycle you might find your confidence and energy levels are at their highest. Sex drive also tends to peak at this time.
Once your period arrives, body temperature drops. You may experience cramps or lingering PMS symptoms such as tiredness or mood swings. Try logging symptoms in the app.

- Follicular phase: {{follicularLength}} ± {{follicularVariation}} days long

- Luteal phase: {{lutealLength}} ± {{lutealVariation}} days long

Most Cyclers have a follicular phase of 17±5 days and luteal phase of 12±2 days.

perimenopause-assessment-body--EARLY: This stage is often characterized by the presence of several symptoms, without significant changes to your cycle.
perimenopause-assessment-body--LATE: This stage is often characterized by less frequent and longer cycles, with average cycle lengths exceeding 60 days.
perimenopause-assessment-body--MENOPAUSE: We know symptoms don’t necessarily stop when your period does. By tracking your experience, you can gain insights and identify patterns to help you navigate your journey.
perimenopause-assessment-body--MIDDLE: Irregular cycles, with variations of 8 or more days and cycle lengths below 21 or above 35 days, are typical of this stage.
perimenopause-assessment-body--NOT_PMP: At this stage, cycles tend to be more regular and symptoms specific to perimenopause may not be present yet. There is so much to learn from tracking your cycle — we can help you spot patterns and notice future irregularities.
perimenopause-assessment-body--UNKNOWN: This might be because we need more information about your cycle history, or you may have indicated a possible condition whose symptoms can overlap with those of perimenopause.
perimenopause-assessment-disclaimer: Your results are here to support you, not diagnose or replace a conversation with your doctor.

perimenopause-tour-last-step: Start your first day with Natural Cycles by logging your experiences. You can update this later if something changes.
perimenopause-tour-step1-tooltip1: You can still be fertile in perimenopause. Use protection or abstain from sex on Red Days.
perimenopause-tour-step1-tooltip2: Checking in on how you feel each day can help you identify patterns and spot potential triggers for your symptoms.

postpartum-tour-step1-tooltip1: You can be fertile even before your period returns. So, if you're resuming sexual activities before the algorithm detects your ovulation, be sure to use protection.
postpartum-tour-step1-tooltip2: Use mood trackers to support your physical and mental recovery and help spot any  patterns.

pregnancy-dates-conception-date-tutorial:
Your conception date is the day you ovulated in your last menstrual cycle, as this is the day the sperm cell met the egg cell. 

Conception dates are usually based on the day your period started, but using your ovulation date instead can give a more precise estimate of when fertilization happened.
How is my conception date calculated?
pregnancy-dates-due-date-tutorial-body:
Your due date is calculated based on your ovulation and conception date. 

This can be more accurate than giving a date based on your last period, but if the app didn’t have enough data to find ovulation, you can manually add it here.
pregnancy-dates-due-date-tutorial-title: How is my due date calculated?
pregnancy-dates-pregnancy-week-tutorial-: Pregnancy weeks are also worked out from the day of your ovulation. Medical professionals will count from the first day of your last period, as they can’t confirm when you ovulated. To match how your doctor or midwife counts, our algorithm automatically adds on 2 extra pregnancy weeks.

reminders-modal-txt:
Reminders help you to stay on track, so you can get the very most out of your Natural Cycles experience.

You can enable and disable reminders in the app individually and anytime.

Please note: In order to receive reminders you need to agree to Natural Cycles sending you notifications in your device settings. If you happen to remove this permission, we will no longer be able to send these reminders to you. Have fun finding out which reminders work best for you!

settings-clearCache-body: Glitches and errors can sometimes happen in the app due to a quantity of unsaved data. This can occur when you switch between devices or change how you use the app. To get a smoother app experience, try clearing your unsaved data.
settings-clearCache-note: **Note!** It’s safe to delete your unsaved data, and this won’t affect any past or future fertility status.
settings-goAnonymous-body: When you Go Anonymous, we separate your personal and fertility data in our database. This means that some features, such as Partner View, are no longer available.
settings-goAnonymous-warning: **Note!** Your data is always protected, but this feature offers another level of protection for those whose data may be at risk.
settings-goal-perimenopause-accordion1-b: You’ll continue seeing Red and Green Days, retaining the benefits of the birth control feature.
settings-goal-perimenopause-accordion1-t: Birth control is part of NC° Perimenopause mode
settings-goal-perimenopause-accordion2-b: Your previous data from other modes is saved when you switch. The algorithm will continue using your temperature and cycle data to provide you with insights.
settings-goal-perimenopause-accordion3-b: If you decide that NC° Perimenopause isn’t right for you now, you can always switch to another mode.
settings-goal-perimenopause-body:
This mode is designed to assess where you are in perimenopause and help you make sense of symptoms and cycle changes.

Good to know before you switch:
settings-goal-warning: **Note:** Changing modes in the app may affect the algorithm. If you switch between modes, keep in mind that some data might look a little different than it did before.
settings-healthData-revoke-body: Without access to your health data the app won’t function. This means we won’t be able to show your fertility status or to give you updates about your cycle.
settings-notifications-app-badge-subtitl: Get notified of updates in the the app via the icon badge on your home screen

settings-science-consent: Natural Cycles can use my health data related to the menstrual cycle, intercourse, medical conditions, pregnancy, birth control choices and any other data entered into the Natural Cycles app for research in women’s reproductive health. Such research is performed using pseudonymized or anonymized data. I can withdraw my consent at any time, as described in the [Privacy Policy](https://www.naturalcycles.com/other/legal/privacy).
settings-science-consent-more: (for more information see ch. 4.3 in our Privacy Policy)
settings-science-consent-policy:
Women's health is important to Natural Cycles and we invest in scientific research in sexual and reproductive health in order to advance women’s health. We also conduct research for the purpose of evaluating the effectiveness and suitability of the App for different user groups. Thirdly we use the results of our research to communicate the benefits and limitations of Natural Cycles to healthcare professionals. All our published research is subjected to independent peer review and has ethical approval from the relevant professional bodies.

If we have your consent, we will use your User Data and other Personal Data that you may provide, such as data related to the menstrual cycle, intercourse, medical conditions, pregnancy, birth control choices and any other data entered into the Natural Cycles app, in pseudonymized or anonymized form whenever possible (see the Glossary in the Privacy Policy for more information on pseudonymization and anonymization), for clinical studies, scientific articles and other research purposes as may be disclosed when your Personal Data is collected. You may withdraw your consent at any time.

Personal Data is anonymized and aggregated before any such publications are shared outside of Natural Cycles (see the Glossary for more information on anonymization). We may also contact you with requests to participate in specific research projects run by us or our business partners.

Natural Cycles also contribute to research carried out by selected universities, institutions and other parties by sharing anonymized and minimized data with them. For the avoidance of doubt, we do not share any Personal Data with such external parties.

Finally, we may analyze sensitive data in order to publicly share insights learned from aggregated data with the purpose of increasing the public knowledge and understanding of women's health and/or the menstrual cycle. This kind of publication is always based on aggregated anonymized data and as such doesn’t contain any personal information.

Please see our [Privacy Policy](https://www.naturalcycles.com/other/legal/privacy) for more information.

switch-device-before-you-switch-body: Here’s what you should know to get the best experience when you change device:
switch-device-before-you-switch-info-bod:
- Your graph will look different until the algorithm adjusts to your new device
- Switch at the start of your cycle to minimize time without a cover line

- NC° is just as effective no matter the type of measuring device that’s used
- But you may get more Red Days, particularly if you switch mid-cycle

- Each device works differently so it’s important you only measure with one
- Frequently switching between devices will result in more Red Days
switch-device-free-therm-body:
If you want to measure orally, you must have a basal thermometer. This is a special thermometer that measures to two decimal places.

A free thermometer is included with your annual membership. Order yours today and start your journey!
switch-device-info-body--APPLE_WATCH:
**Connect your Apple Watch**

If you have a compatible watch, follow the step-by-step instructions to get started.

**Wear your Apple Watch to sleep**

There’s no need to set an alarm - your temperature is measured overnight. 

**Confirm your daily fertility status**

Your temperature will automatically sync to NC° app when you wake up.

[You can buy your Apple Watch here](https://www.apple.com/watch/)
switch-device-info-body--B1:
**Measure seamlessly overnight**

Say goodbye to morning measuring with NC° Band, a new wearable option from NC°. Measure while you sleep for great value with no additional subscription fee. 

**Adapts to your routine**

Designed for maximum comfort and with a generous battery life, NC° Band is all about convenience. Snooze to your heart’s content, or get started early with your day. Whatever your style, simply sync your data when it suits you best.
switch-device-info-body--GARMIN_WATCH:
**Get Garmin x Natural Cycles°**
Sync any compatible Garmin wearable with the Natural Cycles app for a smooth integration that’s built around you.

**Not just for daytime tracking**
Garmin tracks, NC° transforms overnight temperature data into trusted fertility insights you can plan your health around.

**Be one step ahead of your cycle**
You get performance stats with Garmin, now get science-backed insights unique to your cycle with the Natural Cycles app.

[Claim a discount on a new Garmin wearable](/shop/GARMIN_WATCH)
switch-device-info-body--ORAL_THERMOMETE:
**Why a Basal Body Thermometer?**

BBT thermometers take a more specific temperature reading than regular fever thermometers. This is needed to detect the subtle changes that happen during your cycle. 

**How does NC° use my temperature data?**

Natural Cycles is powered by an algorithm that uses your unique temperature data to calculate a fertility status for every single day of your cycle.
switch-device-info-body--OURA:
**Get your mornings back**

No more beeps, no more measuring as soon as you wake up. Just wear your Oura Ring while you sleep and forget about the rest.

**Adapts to your lifestyle**

Irregular sleep? The Natural Cycles algorithm will pick up on it and correct your temperature according to your individual patterns.

**New health insights with the Oura App**

Get to know your body even better with advanced insights around your Sleep, Activity, and beyond.

[Claim a discount on your Oura Ring](/shop/OURA_RING_DISCOUNT)
switch-device-info-body--R1:
**Effortless overnight measuring**  

Discover a new way to measure overnight with NC° Ring, our latest state-of-the-art wearable. Wear while you sleep and sync data in the morning with the NC° app. No extra subscription fees, no third-party apps.

**Lightweight and long-lasting**  

A lighter way to measure and designed for female physiology, NC° Ring offers deep insights into your cycle. Sleek, strong and built to last, enjoy up 14 days of battery life. Ready to get started?
switch-device-info-body--T3_THERMOMETER:
**Sync smoothly with Bluetooth**

Our new Bluetooth thermometers make the measuring experience even smoother. Simply measure in the morning and sync when you’re ready. Each device saves at least 10 temperature readings. 

**Upgrade your measuring routine**

With new features such as an optional beep and backlight, our next generation of thermometers are designed to make mornings easier.
